findings.finding: No route for new supply opens inside the window: about 91% of outstanding shares are held by the WISeQey/SEALSQ group under lock-ups (SEALSQ's PIPE shares until 60 days after a resale registration that has not been filed; WISeQey's distributed shares for six months from closing), EDGAR text search finds no ATM language ever, and nothing has been filed since 2026-10-08.
findings.mechanism_in_window: An offering, ATM draw or resale registration is the commonest second leg down for a fallen small cap; none can price before the 2026-10-13 close, because there is no effective shelf or resale registration (no F-1/F-3 in the filing list) and the large holders are contractually locked. So the usual negative shoe is absent from the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: the name has no history of offerings as a listed company. Its 7 comparable falls since 2026-09-10 (mostly SPAC-era and post-close meme moves) went up 3 times and down 4, median next close -19%, so the absence of supply has not stopped repeat falls.
findings.why_not_priced: The tape cannot tell whether a dilutive filing is coming tonight; a price already holding a raise would show heavier intraday selling than today's -1.3% intraday leg after the gap. It is small because removing one route for a second shoe does not supply a buyer.
findings.independence: The baseline's EDGAR full-text probe finds 0 'at-the-market' hits ever and 0 'minimum bid price' hits (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002101411.json); the PIPE lock-up is also described in the 10-01 closing coverage (https://thequantuminsider.com/?p=2394818)
